title: Adequate affineness survives stack base change over an affine scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $T$ be an affine $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ be algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $f:\mathcal U\to T$ and $h:\mathcal V\to T$ be $k$-morphisms. If $f$ is adequately affine [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism], then the projection $\mathcal U\times_T\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$ from the $2$-fibre product is adequately affine. There is no flatness or representability hypothesis on $h$ and no hypothesis on the diagonals of $\mathcal U$ or $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1(6), printed p.21, specialized to an affine-scheme target (its diagonal is affine and hence quasi-affine). Primary Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 read online; local Alper PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=\mathcal U\times_T\mathcal V$, with projection $p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal V$. The algebraic-stack fibre-product lemma makes $\mathcal P$ an algebraic stack. For every scheme $W\to\mathcal V$, eliminating the redundant $\mathcal V$-object and its specified isomorphism in a triple gives the canonical equivalence $\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal V}W\simeq\mathcal U\times_TW$, compatible with the projections to $W$ and $\mathcal U$. This equivalence also identifies the restricted algebras and their section maps.

By the definition of adequate affineness, $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These conditions pass to $p$ directly from the test definitions: for a quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal V$, one has $\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal V}\mathcal Z\simeq\mathcal U\times_T\mathcal Z$, which is quasi-compact by the test for $f$. Moreover $\Delta_p$ is the pullback of $\Delta_f$ along $\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal V}\mathcal P\to\mathcal U\times_T\mathcal U$. Thus every scheme test of $\Delta_p$ is literally a scheme test of $\Delta_f$, so is an algebraic space with quasi-compact and quasi-separated projection. This proves the two conditions without any assertion about the absolute diagonal of $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Tags 050V (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact) and 050F (lemma-base-change-separated), here proved directly from the test definitions

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary surjection $\alpha:\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal P$. For a smooth scheme test $W\to\mathcal V$ and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal U\times_TW,\mathcal B_W)$, cover $W$ by affine open subschemes $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}S_i$. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The restricted map $\alpha_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B_i$ on $\mathcal U_i=\mathcal U\times_TW_i$ is again a surjection of quasi-coherent algebras. Indeed restriction in the big fppf convention is precomposition: over an object on a scheme $Z$ it leaves the section rings and structure-ring action unchanged. A covering on which a section lifts, or on which a module presentation is exact, lifts to the restricted fibred category by pulling back the additional $W_i$-map on $Z$. Hence the original local surjectivity and local presentations remain valid. This argument applies to every $\alpha$, with no descent-from-$\mathcal U$ requirement.

source.place: Tags 06TP, 06TV and 06WG (inherited topology, structure sheaf and quasi-coherent module); direct restriction argument

proof.text: The projection $q_i:\mathcal U_i\to\mathcal U$ is affine by the affine-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image], applied to $R\to S_i$. That same lemma sends $\alpha_i$ to a surjection $q_{i,\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A_i\twoheadrightarrow q_{i,\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal B_i$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal U$. Its natural ring isomorphisms identify $t|_{W_i}$ with a section of the latter algebra on $\mathcal U$. Since $f$ is adequately affine with affine target, [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion] gives $N_i>0$ and a section of $q_{i,\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A_i$ whose image is that section to the $N_i$-th power. Transfer it back to $s_i\in\Gamma(\mathcal U_i,\mathcal A_i)$. Compatibility of the ring isomorphisms with $\alpha_i$ and powers gives exactly $\alpha_i(s_i)=(t|_{W_i})^{N_i}$.

proof.text: For this arbitrary $\alpha$ and arbitrary smooth test $W\to\mathcal V$, step 4 supplies the required positive-power lifts on the affine open cover $(W_i\to W)$. Such a cover is an etale cover: locally its ring maps are localizations, which are flat and locally finitely presented, and its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence unramified. The direct-image section formula in [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism] and the equivalence of step 1 identify these lifts with sections of $p_*\mathcal A$ mapping to powers of the given section of $p_*\mathcal B$. Thus $p_*\alpha$ is universally adequate in precisely that definition. Together with step 2, this makes $p$ adequately affine. The construction uses arbitrary $h$ and imposes no condition on either absolute diagonal.
